title: recovery_objectives.v1
description: How much data a service may lose, how long it may be down, and the failures it is designed to survive (00_UniversalStandards/16_Service_Design_Record.md §3). rpo_seconds is the most recent window of acknowledged writes the service may lose; rto_seconds is the longest it may be unavailable. Replication does not meet an RPO on its own, because it copies a bad write or delete to every replica. Rules JSON Schema cannot express, enforced by the design record's relationship rules (schemas/design_record_rules.v1.json): every backed-up store's worst-case recovery point is no longer than the RPO (DR-010); a region-scoped failover needs those stores in more than one region (DR-011); no failure scenario takes longer than the RTO (DR-019); and expected downtime from the scenarios fits every availability SLO's budget (DR-020).

scope.description: The largest failure the failover path survives.

procedure.description: Where the runbook is, or how failover happens automatically.

expected_per_year.description: How often the scenario is expected to happen; correct it from incident history.

downtime_seconds.description: Expected unavailability per occurrence, given the failover path.

failure_scenarios.description: The failures the service is designed to survive. Expected downtime from them must fit every availability SLO's budget (DR-020), and none may take longer than the RTO (DR-019).
